Descriptive public-data demonstration

Economic Growth and Women’s Employment in South Asia

Descriptive endpoint comparison of Pakistan, Bangladesh and India, 2010–2024.

Research domain

Economics & Policy

Classification

Work Sample

Evidence

Supplied sample PDF reviewed; original data/scripts unavailable

Coverage

2010–2024

OverviewEvidence & methodsFindingsLimitationsContribution & samples
Work Sample

A sample supported by the supplied documentation, with the contribution and limits to replication explained below.

Project brief

Question

Compare economic growth and women’s employment without confusing coincidence with causality.

Analytical scope

Descriptive endpoint comparison of Pakistan, Bangladesh and India, 2010–2024.

Presented output

A country comparison table, a real GDP per capita growth chart, an employment comparison chart and an interpretation note.

Interpretation

Growth and women’s employment should be reported separately; the supplied changes do not establish a causal link.

The research question

How did economic growth and women’s employment indicators change across three South Asian economies between 2010 and 2024? This descriptive public-data demonstration compares Pakistan, Bangladesh and India to present differences in economic and employment indicators clearly.

Data and analytical scope

The supplied public-data sample uses two indicators from the World Bank’s World Development Indicators (WDI): GDP per capita in constant 2015 US dollars and the female employment-to-population ratio for women aged 15 and over, based on modelled ILO estimates. The comparison presented here uses observations from 2010 and 2024. The PDF describes an annual dataset containing 45 country-year observations and 135 source values. It reports that all requested values were available and that no imputation or smoothing was applied. These are reported dataset characteristics, not independently verified counts on this website. The comparison is not a population-weighted regional average.

The analysis is descriptive. It compares percentage changes in real GDP per capita and changes in female employment-to-population ratios between the two years. Changes in employment ratios are expressed in percentage points. No regression models, causal estimates or observations for the intervening years are presented.

Three economies, different endpoint changes

Supplied endpoint comparisons, 2010–2024
CountryReal GDP per capita growth (%)Female employment ratio, 2010 (%)Female employment ratio, 2024 (%)Change (percentage points)
Pakistan30.1121.89522.228+0.333
Bangladesh105.7234.17137.374+3.203
India91.6226.23831.090+4.852

Among the three countries, Bangladesh recorded the largest increase in real GDP per capita (105.72%), followed by India (91.62%) and Pakistan (30.11%). Female employment-to-population ratios increased by 3.203 percentage points in Bangladesh, 4.852 in India and 0.333 in Pakistan. India has the largest employment-ratio increase among the three countries, while Bangladesh has the highest female employment ratio in both 2010 and 2024.

What this comparison cannot establish

Differences between the two years do not reveal trends within the 2010–2024 period, the drivers of change or a causal relationship between growth and employment. Modelled estimates have methodological limitations. The supplied PDF documents retrieval on 14 October 2026 and a World Bank API database update on 8 October 2026. Raw API responses and the companion dataset were not supplied here, so the website presents verified endpoint summaries and does not reconstruct annual observations.

Contribution and available samples

This public-data portfolio exercise was prepared for Asif Hussain’s review with AI assistance, as disclosed in the supplied PDF. This is a portfolio demonstration, not a previously published study or a commissioned client assignment. The PDF states that the Python calculations were run and checked. It also states that the accompanying Stata script still requires review and execution in Stata. Those scripts and raw source files are not supplied here; the website does not claim an independent rerun or sole authorship by Asif Hussain.

Source detail and interpretationWDI indicator codes: NY.GDP.PCAP.KD (GDP per capita); SL.EMP.TOTL.SP.FE.ZS (female employment ratio); SL.EMP.TOTL.SP.MA.ZS (male employment ratio). The PDF reports rounded 2024 male–female gaps of 53.9, 40.2 and 43.2 percentage points for Pakistan, Bangladesh and India. GDP per capita is an average output measure, not median household income, and constant-dollar values are not PPP-adjusted. Changes in the age composition of the population aged 15 and over can affect these ratios.

Source document reviewed privately. Download withheld pending sharing approval.

The PDF mentions a companion ZIP containing raw data and scripts; that archive was not supplied and is not offered as a download.
